alt: Poster: 0.005% stamp duty on mutual fund unit purchases; covers lump sum, SIP, switch-in/STP and IDCW reinvestment; not charged on redemption; units allotted net of duty
text:
A mutual fund purchase is not credited rupee for rupee: stamp duty is taken out first.

Since 1 July 2020, stamp duty of 0.005% applies to mutual fund unit purchases, under Notification S.O. 1226(E) dated 30 March 2020 read with Part I of Chapter IV of the Finance Act, 2019. It covers lump sum purchases, SIP instalments, switch-ins (including STP) and IDCW reinvestment. It is not charged on redemptions or switch-outs.

The duty is recovered from the investor's subscription amount, and units are allotted only on the balance. On a Rs 1,00,000 purchase that works out to roughly Rs 5, so units are issued for about Rs 99,995 at the applicable NAV.

Our view: the amount is small, but it is one more reason the amount invested and the amount that buys units are not identical figures. That is an interpretation, not advice.

For practitioners: how do you explain net-of-duty unit allotment when clients compare their SIP debit with the units shown in the statement?
